heading: Patent — what is patentable
title: Is it patentable? — applying the three tests
rows: 'The idea of paying by mobile phone'
A pure idea — fails industrial applicability
A genuinely new, faster momo-steamer design
Adding an obvious 'share' button to an app
Fails inventiveness — obvious to an expert
A law of nature / gravity formula
A machine already sold in India last year
note: Popularity or cleverness is irrelevant — an invention must be new, non-obvious, AND useful/makeable. Pure ideas, discoveries, and laws of nature fail outright.

heading: Trade Secret — definition
title: Is it a trade secret? — what qualifies and what doesn't
rows: Wai Wai / CG Foods' exact masala ratio
A remittance firm's internal pricing model
Secret info giving a competitive edge
A company's phone number on its website
The patent disclosed it — no longer secret
A software house's private source-code repo
Secret for over a century, never filed
note: It's a trade secret only if it's genuinely confidential AND kept secret by reasonable effort. Anything already public — or disclosed by a patent — cannot be one.

rows: Developer emails the company's source code to a rival

General know-how is theirs to reuse

Breach of the NDA / confidentiality clause

Bribing an insider for a customer list

note: The law protects against misappropriation (theft/breach), not independent discovery or legal reverse engineering — and only if the owner made reasonable efforts to keep it secret.

heading: Open Source Code
title: Is it a licence violation? — MIT/Apache vs GPL in practice
rows: Ships GPL code inside a closed proprietary app
Copyleft requires derivatives be open too

Modifies GPL code, releases the source under GPL

Removes GPL notices and sells it as their own
Copyright infringement of the licensed code
note: Open source is copyright + a licence. Permissive (MIT/Apache) needs attribution; copyleft (GPL) needs derivatives kept open. Breaking either is copyright infringement.
